title: Merge loop invariant
statement: Let $L$ and $R$ be lists of integers, let $[?]$ be a memory map, let $a,b,d$ be natural-number addresses, and let $i,j$ be natural numbers. A state satisfies the invariant if there are a memory map $[?]'$ and an output list $O$ such that its location component is the frame determined by $a,|L|,b,|R|,d,i,j$ and its memory component is $[?]'$; moreover, $i\le |L|$, $j\le |R|$, the two maps agree outside the destination region of length $|L|+|R|$, $|O|=i+j$, $O$ occupies a memory segment beginning at $d$, and concatenating $O$ with the merge of the unconsumed tails of $L$ and $R$ gives the merge of $L$ and $R$.
hypotheses_covered: there exist a modified memory map and an output list
state equals the specified frame paired with the modified map
i is at most the left-list length
j is at most the right-list length
original and modified maps agree outside the destination region
output is a memory segment at the destination
output followed by the merge of the remaining tails equals the merge of the original lists
caveat: The payload omits the definitions of State, frame, SameOutside, Seg, and merge, so some components cannot be specified exactly.
